title: Looking for your critique on SFX and UI in my game
author: zloy_molo4nik
selftext:
Hello!

I'm back with another piece of my game. I recorded a video of the current mechanics and some gameplay.

I'm looking for honest, maybe negative 😄, feedback on the SFX, the UI layouts and the general look and feel.

Please ignore the texts for now, they're my pain 😄 I still need to revise and rewrite all of them myself, so they don't read like slop.

  
To be honest, developing the game has become more difficult now, as the addition of new systems has come to a halt. I’ve entered a phase focused on fixing bugs and adding "juice" to the visual effects and the UI. Don’t mistake this for the final stage before release; I’m working in iterations. However, my perspective has become a bit dulled - it’s hard to tell what feels just right and what stands out too much, clashing with the overall style.

\[Text in this post translated with Google Translate from my native language\]

  
Thank you for your feedback.

comments.author: Xinnobun
comments.body: Keep pushing. This is usually around the time a lot of people give up because its a mess filled with bugs. The SFX is good so far, as long as you have an audio adjuster in the menu options, because sometimes it could be a little too low.

replies.author: zloy_molo4nik
replies.body:
Thanks for the reply. I don’t intend to stop. Even if the game doesn’t reach the necessary sales figures or user numbers, I will still gain valuable experience in developing and marketing my own game.

A special thanks for the tip regarding sound. Yes, I do have separate settings for sound effects (SFX) and the overall game audio. It looks like I’ll need to perform some profiling on the sounds and music tracks as well.

comments.author: ef0uro
comments.body: The overall UI feels super cohesive! It fits the vibe really well.
